## Impact

Customers that have a schema with a caveat using the `in_cidr` function, such as the following

```python
caveat is_valid_ip(user_ip ipaddress, cidr string) {
    user_ip.in_cidr(cidr)
  }
```

can get different results for two textual forms of the same IPv4 host. An allow-list (permit when `in_cidr` is true) fails closed for a mapped address; a deny-style check (negating `in_cidr`, or granting extra access for internal ranges) fails open.

In other words, the following .zed file fails the second assertion:

```yaml
---
schema: |+
  definition user {}

  caveat is_valid_ip(user_ip ipaddress, cidr string) {
    user_ip.in_cidr(cidr)
  }

  definition document {
  	relation viewer: user with is_valid_ip
    permission view = viewer
  }

relationships: >-
  document:firstdoc#viewer@user:alice[is_valid_ip:{"cidr":"10.0.0.0/8"}]
assertions:
  assertTrue:
    - 'document:firstdoc#view@user:alice with {"user_ip": "10.1.2.3"}'
    - 'document:firstdoc#view@user:alice with {"user_ip": "::ffff:a01:203"}'

```

## Patches

v1.54.1

## Workarounds

Do not use the `in_cidr` caveat function.

### Update 2026-09-07

This advisory is published but has no CVE ID. GitHub does not assign one automatically, and the request needs admin on the advisory, which I do not have as the reporter. It is the "Request CVE" button, or

    POST /repos/authzed/spicedb/security-advisories/GHSA-5784-6qcr-48fq/cve

Would you be willing to do that? The details a record needs are below. I have not scored it; the severity and the CVSS vector are yours to set. If you would rather not request one, tell me and I will ask MITRE instead, which is open to me now that the advisory is public.

    Product: github.com/authzed/spicedb
    CWE: CWE-697 (Incorrect Comparison)
    Description: The in_cidr caveat treats an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address as a
    different address family from its dotted form, so the same host evaluates
    differently depending on how the caller spells it. Caveats gate the
    permission decision, so an IP allow/deny list built on in_cidr can be evaded.
    Verified against: 7a1e5cce428f0709e92fdb037c0944d82d4e0212
